subject: AthenaOps SLA adaptation proposal — latency commitment and operational mapping
messages:
From: Alicia Moreno <alicia@athenaops.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 15:14:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed SLA for strategic deployment (AthenaOps)

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks again for the conversation earlier this week. AthenaOps is ready to move forward with Redwood for our inference layer, but the board has asked for an explicit latency commitment for peak-policy inference attached to the contract. We discussed a p95 target of 75ms for our production traffic (90th percentile at peak) with a defined burst window of up to 10k RPS sustained for 30s during scheduled releases.

Attached is our baseline SLA draft (athenaops-proposed-sla-v2.pdf) and a short runbook showing expected request shapes (athena-runbook-draft.xlsx). Key asks:
- p95 inference latency <= 75ms for the primary model (context length ~512)
- documented operational response plan for degraded states (who will be paged, escalation cadence)
- fallback model with sub-150ms p95 if the primary variant is unavailable

We understand there are cost and architecture tradeoffs; we are prepared to discuss reserved capacity or a blended pricing approach. Can you confirm what information you need from us to evaluate an exception/commitment? Also include any timeline constraints from your side — Athena would like this in place before our H1 GA (target: 2027-08-15).

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Moreno
Head of Platform Engineering | AthenaOps
Attachments: athenaops-proposed-sla-v2.pdf (PDF, 92KB), athena-runbook-draft.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia@athenaops.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA for strategic deployment (AthenaOps)

Alicia — thanks for the clear deck and runbook. Looping in product (Karthik), eng (Marissa), and legal/enterprise (Lauren) to scope feasibility and the approval path.

Quick notes from my side:
- We can evaluate a p95_75ms commitment but need to validate traffic shape assumptions and whether AthenaOps will take Dedicated or Hosted with reserved pools. The difference is material to both cost and feasibility.
- For burst behavior (10k RPS for 30s), we need the inter-arrival distribution. Is that a hard SLA condition or a planning envelope?
- Operational expectations: please confirm on-call rotations and whether Athena wants Redwood on-call escalation for the first 6 weeks after GA.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal feasibility: product/infra to confirm if the runtime can meet p95 75ms for your model + token sizes under the projected RPS (Karthik/Marissa).
2) Costing: finance/procurement to model a dedicated pool vs. burst credits (Lauren and I can run this once we have numbers).
3) Operational runbook alignment: sync call next week to walk the runbook and escalation lines.

Can Karthik/Marissa weigh in on the feasibility and whether a fallback-model SLA (sub-150ms p95) is realistic as a contractual fallback? I would like to get an internal decision before the week is out — Athena's timeline is tight.

—Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, Alicia Moreno <alicia@athenaops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA for strategic deployment (AthenaOps)

Thanks — I reviewed the runbook. A few follow-ups from product side:

1) Model & context: we need the exact model family and typical input/output token counts. The runbook shows median inputs of ~220 tokens but peaks up to ~1400. If peak sequence length is truly 1400, that changes kernel selection and latency profile significantly.

2) p95 target: 75ms p95 for a 512-context workload is plausible on our optimized runtime if the model is quantized and served from a dedicated pool with CPU/GPU carefully provisioned. For 1400 tokens, we should expect ~2–3x latency unless we shard differently.

3) Burst handling: Redwood has a burst fabric (cross-tenant borrowing) but contractual commitments for burst windows require reserved capacity or explicit credit allotments. We can propose a blended model: baseline reserved capacity to cover steady-state + burst credits that convert to on-demand pooled capacity. That will still require an operational playbook for pre-scheduled high-volume events.

I've attached an internal draft runbook template with where we need Athena inputs (athena-runbook-draft.xlsx).

Operational asks for contractual fallback: we can commit to a fallback model at sub-150ms p95 if Athena accepts that fallback is functionally equivalent for degraded scenarios. We should define metrics to detect fallback and a max switch duration (e.g., fallback transitions must be completed within 10s of threshold breach).

Marissa — can engineering provide a rough latency curve (p50/p95/p99) for 512 vs 1400 token contexts and clarify what quantization levels we can support without severe quality degradation?

Karthik
Principal Product Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachments: internal-runbook-template.md (referenced), athena-runbook-draft.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, Alicia Moreno <alicia@athenaops.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA for strategic deployment (AthenaOps)

Quick engineering read — we can meet the 75ms p95 for a 512-context model on a dedicated ampere-class pool with quantized weights (4-bit or 8-bit, depending on quality tolerance). Notes:

- 512 tokens, optimized kernel, dedicated pool: estimated p95 = 50–80ms depending on batch coalescing and KV cache hit rate.
- 1400 tokens: estimated p95 = 140–220ms on the same hardware. To get under 75ms at 1400 tokens we'd need model parallelism and higher-cost hardware, which has material cost implications.
- Burst of 10k RPS for 30s: that is significant. If Athena can schedule major releases or declare maintenance windows, we can provision a temporary burst pool. For unscheduled bursts we'd rely on cross-tenant pooling and credits, not guaranteed by SLA.

Questions for Athena:
1) Can you confirm the real maximum sequence length we must optimize for?
2) Are you willing to accept quantized model variants (we'd include an eval comparing outputs at 4-bit/8-bit to current baseline)?
3) Do you prefer a contractual fallback (sub-150ms p95) for degraded states or a phased operational escalation with partial credits?

If the answers line up, I can put together a cost delta for Dedicated 3x nodes vs. a baseline hosted + burst credits approach. We should model both run rates for your finance team.

—Marissa
Director, Inference Engineering | Redwood Inference
Attachment referenced: engineering-latency-estimates.csv (summary table)

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA for strategic deployment (AthenaOps)

Team — great alignment so far. Summary and proposed internal asks for approval:

Summary of agreed approach for discussion with AthenaOps:
- Baseline: commit to p95 <= 75ms for 512-context on Dedicated reserved pool (details: 3 nodes of A100-equivalent, quantized to 4/8-bit depending on Athena QA).
- Fallback: contractual fallback to a validated sub-150ms p95 model variant for degraded states; fallback switch must be executable within 10s of threshold breach and is expected to be used only under capacity stress/event windows.
- Burst handling: scheduled high-load windows will be covered by temporary reserved capacity (customer to notify 48h ahead). Unscheduled bursts will use burst credits with best-effort behavior (explicitly excluded from hard SLA).
- Operational: Redwood will provide a joint runbook; post-GA we will offer 6 weeks of high-touch support (during which Redwood on-call may be paged for incidents related to the commitment).

Internal asks / approvals needed:
1) Product sign-off on fallback switch behavior and quality guardrails (Karthik).
2) Engineering cost delta and feasibility sign-off to confirm the 3-node config and any additional ops staffing (Marissa).
3) Legal review for SLA phrasing and fallback enforcement clauses (Lauren).
4) Sales exec approval for a limited-term exception to our standard availability SLOs (this will need a C-level sign-off given the exposure).

I propose we collect the above signoffs by end-of-week (2027-07-02) so I can respond to Athena with a redline-ready commitment and term sheet. I'll draft the doc for legal once Karthik/Marissa confirm their points.

If anyone has redlines to the summary, reply-all with line numbers and I'll consolidate.

—Nikhil
Senior Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced for Athena: athenaops-proposed-sla-v2.pdf, athena-runbook-draft.xlsx, engineering-latency-estimates.csv
